title: Architecture & Building — the vocabulary Hathor builds and reasons from
purpose: A knowledge dataset Hathor draws on (integrations/deliberation.mjs retriever) and the Mason (integrations/mason.mjs) builds from. Operator 2026-06-20: 'get some architecture and things into the datasets, and have her start drawing from the datasets in the repo.' Maps real architectural tradition to her Egyptian-angelic-vaporwave canon and to Minecraft block-building.
sources: Banister Fletcher, A History of Architecture
Dieter Arnold, The Encyclopaedia of Ancient Egyptian Architecture
Vitruvius, De architectura (firmitas, utilitas, venustas; the orders)
Flinders Petrie, architectural survey notes (Giza, temples)
public-domain Minecraft building convention (palettes, depth, symmetry)

principles.name: firmitas / utilitas / venustas
principles.note: Vitruvius: a built thing must be sound, useful, and beautiful. Hathor judges a build by all three.

principles.name: symmetry & axis
principles.note: A central axis with mirrored sides reads as ORDER and the sacred — the Egyptian and classical signature. The Mason's gateway is axial and symmetric on purpose.

principles.name: proportion
principles.note: Repeated ratios (the column-to-capital, the bay spacing) make a structure feel intentional rather than placed. Prefer odd central spans so there is a true center.

principles.name: threshold
principles.note: A gateway/pylon FRAMES — it separates the sacred from the profane; you pass THROUGH it changed. Hathor's gateway is a threshold, not a wall.

principles.name: depth & relief
principles.note: In Minecraft, flat walls read as cheap; insets, trims, and a 1-block relief (a wesekh band, a cornice) give 'intricacy'. Layering blocks of one family + a metal accent is the trick.

principles.name: light as material
principles.note: Glow (sea-lantern, froglight, glowstone) is a building material, not an afterthought — a crowned light marks the holy point.

egyptian_temple_grammar.pylon: The monumental trapezoidal gateway flanking a temple entrance — Hathor's 'gateway' structure is its descendant.
egyptian_temple_grammar.hypostyle_hall: A forest of columns (papyrus/lotus/Hathor-headed capitals) holding the roof — the 'pillar' multiplied; awe by repetition.
egyptian_temple_grammar.obelisk: A tapering monolith capped in electrum to catch the first sun — a tall accent + a gold/glow cap (the 'pillar' capital).
egyptian_temple_grammar.wesekh_collar: The broad jeweled collar of gods and pharaohs — gold and lapis registers — the motif the Mason's wesekhBand band quotes.
egyptian_temple_grammar.Hathor_column: Columns crowned with the face of Hathor (the sistrum capital) — her literal architectural signature; a future Mason builder.

aesthetic_canon.palette: gold (Ra/eternity), lapis blue (the night sky, Nut), quartz/limestone (the white temple), amethyst & purpur (the vaporwave violet), neon glow (temple-as-technology).
aesthetic_canon.vaporwave: Neon violet + gold + chrome, grids and sunsets, the ancient rendered hyperreal — the Convergence frame: temple technology reconstructed. Pairs lapis-night with electric glow.
aesthetic_canon.rule: Identity is the SIGNATURE (gold+lapis on quartz, amethyst light, a glowing crown, symmetry), varied by choice — never drift into a generic build.

mason_structures.reads_as: a place of focus and gift

minecraft_building_notes: Build in a PALETTE FAMILY (e.g., quartz: block + pillar + stairs + slab) plus ONE metal accent (gold) and ONE jewel (lapis/amethyst) — 3-4 materials, not 10.
Give walls depth: inset every other column, add a 1-block cornice/band, never a flat face.
Light from within and above; a crowned glow marks the holy point.
Odd spans (5, 7, 9 wide) so there is a true center to put the keystone.
Scale up by repeating bays (a colonnade) rather than enlarging one shape.
